title: How Not To Run an A/B Test (Evan Miller, 18 April 2010)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Peeking inflates false positives (worked example: 26.1% where 5% was intended); fix the sample size in advance; rule of thumb n = 16 sigma squared / delta squared, with sigma squared = p(1 - p) for a conversion rate.

title: Sample Size Calculator (Evan's Awesome A/B Tools)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Inputs (baseline rate, minimum detectable effect as absolute or relative, power, significance level) and output (sample size per variation).

title: Simple Sequential A/B Testing (Evan Miller, 13 October 2015)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The stopping rule (stop when treatment minus control successes reaches 2 times the square root of N, or total successes reach N), one-sided 5% basis, about 2.25 root N for two-sided, and when it saves sample.

title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, Ya Xu; Cambridge University Press, 2020)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The book's authors, publisher and year, and its emphasis on an Overall Evaluation Criterion (OEC).

title: Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in Online Controlled Experiments: A Taxonomy and Rules of Thumb for Practitioners (KDD 2019)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page lists Aleksander Fabijan). What a sample ratio mismatch is, why ignoring it can ship a bad change, and a taxonomy drawn from four companies and 25+ products.

title: Patterns of Trustworthy Experimentation: Pre-Experiment Stage (31 July 2020)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Falsifiable hypothesis, core metric set with guardrails, power analysis, randomisation unit (cookies unstable), retrospective A/A checks, progressive rollout.

title: Patterns of Trustworthy Experimentation: During-Experiment Stage (25 January 2021)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. SRMs typically invalidate a test; alerts and auto-shutdown on guardrails (a Bing test that introduced a 404 page); novelty effects (a 28% click lift on a Microsoft News button that faded); stricter significance for early looks; stable segments.

title: Patterns of Trustworthy Experimentation: Post-Experiment Stage (24 December 2021)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Check set-up against intended allocation; triggered analysis; trading off OEC and guardrails with weights set in advance; rerun results that look too good (Twyman's law); archive tests.

title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 7.3.3: How can we determine whether two processes produce the same proportion of defectives?
publisher: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Two-proportion z-test with a pooled proportion for large samples; Fisher's exact test for small samples.

title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 1.3.5.15: Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit Test
publisher: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The chi-square goodness-of-fit statistic (sum of (observed - expected) squared / expected) and the need for enough expected counts.

title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 7.4.7.3: Bonferroni's method
publisher: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Bonferroni: for g comparisons chosen in advance, use alpha / g for each to keep overall confidence at least 1 - alpha.

title: Statistical significance (Optimizely Experimentation docs, dated 5 August 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Stats Engine accounts for running time, uses false discovery rate control with two-tailed tests, applies no extra FDR control across segments, holds winners until minimum visitors and conversions; significance level is a setting.

title: Minimize A/B testing impact in Google Search
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page undated in fetch). No cloaking; rel=canonical on test URLs; 302 not 301 redirects; end tests promptly and remove test code.

title: Google Optimize and Optimize 360 sunset
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Optimize ended on 30 September 2023; Google works with third-party testing tools (AB Tasty, Optimizely, VWO) and opened its APIs.

title: Shopify Editions Winter '26
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Rollouts: scheduled theme changes and A/B tests built into the Shopify admin. No help article on Rollouts could be found to confirm plans or limits.

title: Why You Only Need to Test with 5 Users (Jakob Nielsen, 18 March 2000)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. About 85% of usability problems found with five users (model-based), several small rounds beat one large one, more users for distinct groups and for quantitative studies.

title: Cart Abandonment Rate Statistics (updated 28 October 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 70.22% average documented abandonment from 50 studies (2006 to 2025); reasons for abandonment among US online shoppers (extra costs 40%, slow delivery 20%, trust 19%, forced account 18%, long checkout 17%, errors 17%).

title: Checkout Optimization: Reduce the Number of Form Fields (Edward Scott, 26 June 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Average checkout has 11.3 form fields (2024); most sites need only 8; shares of sites not using single name field (89%), hidden address line 2 (75%), delayed account creation (84%).

title: Web Vitals (updated 31 October 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Core Web Vitals and good thresholds (LCP 2.5 s, INP 200 ms, CLS 0.1) at the 75th percentile; INP replaced FID in 2024.

title: Fogg Behavior Model
supports: Opened with WebFetch. B = MAP: a behaviour happens when motivation, ability and a prompt come together; if it does not happen, one is missing.

title: Guidelines 2/2023 on Technical Scope of Art. 5(3) of ePrivacy Directive, Version 2.0 (adopted 7 October 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF; text extracted). Art. 5(3) protects information on a device whether or not it is personal data (para 10, quoting the CJEU); JavaScript that tells the browser to send information is gaining access (para 33); pixels and unique identifiers are covered.

title: Guidelines 05/2020 on consent under Regulation 2016/679, Version 1.1 (adopted 4 May 2020)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF; text extracted). Cookie walls make consent not freely given (paras 39-40); scrolling or swiping is never consent (para 86); pre-ticked boxes invalid; withdrawal as easy as giving (paras 113-114).

title: Cookies : solutions pour les outils de mesure d'audience (4 July 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (French page). Conditions for audience measurement without consent in France: publisher-only purpose, anonymous statistics, no combining or cross-site tracking; recommended 13-month cookie life and 25-month data retention. Session replay, heatmaps and A/B testing are not mentioned.

title: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025: data protection and privacy changes (first published 27 June 2025)
publisher: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (GOV.UK)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The Act allows storage and access technologies without consent in certain low-risk situations (not named on the page); changes commence in stages 2 to 12 months after Royal Assent on 19 June 2025.

title: About consent mode (Google Analytics Help)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated). Consent mode passes consent choices to Google tags; analytics_storage denied means no analytics cookies; basic mode blocks tags until consent; advanced mode sends cookieless pings used for modelling; set defaults by region.

title: Clarity Cookie Consent API - ConsentV2 (updated 5 December 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. From 31 October 2025 Clarity enforces consent signals for visits from the EEA, UK and Switzerland; without consent it runs with no cookies and a unique ID per page view.

title: Masking content (Microsoft Clarity, updated 5 December 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Masking modes strict, balanced (default) and relaxed; input boxes and drop-downs masked in all modes; masked content is never uploaded; changes are not retroactive; only admins change masking.

title: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) (updated 28 August 2026)
publisher: State of California Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Consumer rights to know, delete, opt out of sale or sharing and limit use of sensitive data; a user-enabled global privacy control must be honoured as an opt-out by covered businesses.

title: The Digital Services Act (policy page, last updated 1 October 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The DSA bans deceptive dark-pattern designs on online platforms; micro and small companies have lighter requirements.
